intro: Investor ITAS (Izin Tinggal Terbatas) is an official limited stay permit issued to foreign nationals who make investments in Indonesia. Unlike a Work KITAS, the holder of an Investor ITAS is not permitted to actively work at the company — they act solely as shareholders and investors. This 1-year permit provides the legal basis for foreign investors to oversee their investments, attend board meetings, and manage their Indonesian business interests.

requirements.item: Original passport with minimum 18 months validity
Company deed of establishment showing applicant's shareholding
Proof of investment / company registration documents
Other identity documents as per immigration requirements

faqs.question: What is the difference between Investor ITAS and Work KITAS?
faqs.answer: Investor ITAS is for shareholders who do not actively work in the company — they can only oversee their investment. Work KITAS is for foreign employees who actively work and receive a salary from an Indonesian company. The Work KITAS requires DPKK and RPTKA approvals, while the Investor ITAS does not.

faqs.question: How long does Investor ITAS processing take?
faqs.answer: Estimated processing time is around 2–4 working weeks after all documents are declared complete by immigration. VERALEX CONSULTING handles the entire process and provides regular status updates.

faqs.question: Can an Investor ITAS holder open a bank account in Indonesia?
faqs.answer: Yes. Official e-ITAS holders can open bank accounts in Indonesia by presenting the ITAS card as proof of legal stay status. Most major banks in Indonesia accept e-ITAS for account opening.

faqs.question: Can family members stay in Indonesia with an Investor ITAS holder?
faqs.answer: Yes. Spouse and children can apply for a Family ITAS (dependent permit) sponsored by the Investor ITAS holder. This allows the entire family to reside in Indonesia legally.

faqs.question: Can Investor ITAS be converted to Work KITAS?
faqs.answer: Converting from Investor ITAS to Work KITAS requires a new application process. The investor would need to obtain DPKK approval and RPTKA from the Ministry of Manpower. We can assist with the conversion process.

faqs.question: What happens if my Investor ITAS expires?
faqs.answer: If your ITAS expires, you must leave Indonesia or apply for an extension before the expiry date. A 60-day grace period may apply, but overstaying results in fines and potential deportation. It is strongly recommended to renew well before the deadline.
